Explanation:  
The question asks how many seasons later an Ixodes scapularis nymph, after feeding in the spring and becoming an adult in the same year, would be likely to transmit Lyme disease. The ground truth answer is "Two seasons," which means transmission would most likely happen in the fall (spring → summer → fall = two seasons after spring). The predicted answer states transmission would occur "in the fall of that same year—about one season later" after feeding in spring. This is incorrect because from spring to fall is two seasons (spring to summer is one season, summer to fall is another).

Decision: FALSE
